title.narrative: Immediate Life-Saving Assistance through Conditional and Unconditional Cash Transfers for the most vulnerable drought affected and displaced communities in Qansax-Dhere District, Bay region.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project aims to deliver immediate, life-saving assistance to vulnerable drought-affected and displaced households in Qansax Dheere, Bay Region—one of four priority districts under the SHF Standard Allocation 1 – 2025. Implemented by AMARD under the Food Security and Emergency ltbgtLivelihoods (FSL) cluster, this intervention addresses critical food insecurity and livelihood collapselt/bgt in a context marked by IPC Phase 4 (Emergency) classification, according to the March 2025 IPC analysis.ltbrgtHouseholds in Qansax Dheere face worsening conditions due to prolonged drought, flash flooding, insecurity, and mass displacement. Rising food prices, loss of productive assets, and limited income opportunities have forced many to adopt negative coping strategies, such as child labor, early marriage, and skipping meals. ltbgtVulnerable groups—including female-headed households, the elderly, persons with disabilities (PWDs), pregnant and lactating women (PLWs), and marginalized minorities—are at heightened risk of exclusion and exploitation.lt/bgtltbrgtIn response, AMARD proposes a cash-based intervention with a total budget of USD 300,000, targeting approximately 5,670 individuals (around 945 households). The assistance will include:ltbrgtUnconditional Cash Transfers (UCT): Targeting the most vulnerable households with $55/month for 3 months to enable access to food and essential non-food items.ltbrgtConditional Cash Transfers (Cash-for-Work): Engaging able-bodied individuals in labor-intensive public works to rehabilitate key infrastructure (e.g., feeder roads, irrigation canals, and water catchments), while generating short-term income and building resilience.ltbrgtThis dual-modality approach responds to urgent food needs while supporting early livelihood recovery and stimulating the local economy. All transfer values align with the Somalia Cash Working Group’s ltbgtMinimum Expenditure Basket (MEB) guidance.lt/bgtltbrgtBeneficiary selection will be based on clear vulnerability criteria, including:ltbrgtlt/pgtltolgtltligtSevere food insecurity (Phase 4),lt/ligtltligtDisplacement status (protracted and recent IDPs),lt/ligtltligtGender (female-headed HHs),lt/ligtltligtAge (elderly caregivers, adolescent-headed HHs),lt/ligtltligtDisability and chronic illness,lt/ligtltligtExposure to GBV or social exclusion (minority clans).lt/ligtlt/olgtltpgtTargeting will follow a transparent, participatory process involving community leaders, women’s groups, minority representatives, and trained protection focal points. AMARD will conduct ltbgthousehold-level registration and verification using sex- and age-disaggregated data (SADD), displacement status, and vulnerability scoring.lt/bgt Lists will be validated through community feedback sessions, cross-checked with humanitarian coordination platforms, and securely stored. Deduplication and fraud mitigation will be ensured through internal controls and local monitoring.ltbrgtTo uphold protection and accountability, the project embeds the following:ltbrgtlt/pgtltulgtltligtA multilingual ltbgtComplaint and Feedback Mechanism (CFM) lt/bgtaccessible by phone, in person, or through partner structureslt/ligtltligtDissemination of ltbgtPSEA and Code of Conduct messages through inclusive IEC materialslt/bgtlt/ligtltligtCoordination with Area-Based Coordination (ABC) mechanisms and referral networks for GBV, disability, and legal services.lt/ligtlt/ulgtltpgtThis intervention contributes directly to SHF 2025 objectives by reducing humanitarian suffering, supporting protection outcomes, and ensuring dignified access to assistance in hard-to-reach, underserved areas. It complements existing SHF-funded initiatives and advances the collective humanitarian response outlined in the 2025 Humanitarian Needs Response Plan (HNRP) and the Centrality of Protection Strategy (2025–2026).ltbrgtlt/pgt
